author: Teresa Elena Frontado
description:
US President Donald Trump said on Monday that Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang had told him he did not know a woman at the centre of espionage allegations was a suspected Chinese spy, and that he believed the technology executive’s account.
Speaking to reporters at the White House, Trump said he had spoken to Huang earlier in the day, as the chipmaker faces scrutiny over whether its founder was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation.
“I asked him that question. Did you have any idea...
title: Trump backs Nvidia’s Huang over spy allegations, says Xi may raise case

author: Han Li,Teresa Elena Frontado
description:
Growing bipartisan pressure is mounting in the US Congress on Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang over his ties to a businesswoman suspected by US intelligence officials of working for Beijing’s intelligence services, with lawmakers from both parties demanding to know whether US national security was compromised.
Chinese authorities have dismissed the spying allegations.
The controversy escalated over the weekend when Nvidia’s board announced an independent investigation after Huang admitted he...
title: US Congress ramps up pressure on Nvidia’s Jensen Huang over alleged China spy links

author: Laura Zhou
description:
Days after three Russian data centres were hit by Ukrainian drone attacks last month – paralysing taxi, delivery and payment apps across Central Asia – Tajikistan launched an internet link between its capital Dushanbe and Beijing.
The optical fibre, which runs through the Pamir Mountains, offers a direct link to Hong Kong – one of the largest internet traffic exchange points in the Asia-Pacific – and marks Tajikistan’s fifth international communication access point.
To the west, Kazakhstan and...
title: Escaping Russia’s web: Central Asia is caught between Chinese networks and US tech curbs

author: Liu Zhen
description:
China has released new images of its GJ-11 stealth combat drone, offering a closer look at the advanced design and high-performance features of the next-generation uncrewed aircraft.
The images appeared on Monday in a report by state broadcaster CCTV counting down to the 77th anniversary of the PLA Air Force on Wednesday.
For the first time, viewers were given a close-up look at the GJ-11’s large internal weapon bay, highlighting its serrated edges. The design suggests that the drone can house...
title: Fresh GJ-11 footage gives a glimpse of weapon bay on China’s next-gen drone

author: Finbarr Bermingham
description:
The government of Lithuania asked Taipei to change the name of a controversial representative office in Vilnius before Beijing’s National Day last month, according to explosive media reports in the tiny Baltic state.
The twist comes as Vilnius seeks to restore diplomatic ties with Beijing, which have been frozen since the opening of the office in 2021.
Reports in Delfi, a Lithuanian news portal, on Monday said a deputy foreign minister delivered a letter to Taipei’s representatives – including...
title: Lithuania asked Taipei to change name of office before Beijing’s National Day: reports

author: Carol Yang
description:
Donald Trump has floated the idea of a trilateral summit with China and Russia to broker an end to the Iran war, with his administration under pressure to deliver a breakthrough following the US midterm elections, according to analysts.
Chinese observers also see Beijing potentially playing the role of a neutral mediator and offering a diplomatic platform rather than pressuring Tehran into a deal.
Speaking to reporters on Sunday, the US president said he would meet his Chinese and Russian...
title: Can Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin give Donald Trump the Iran exit he needs?

author: Caroline Lin
description:
China has been the backdrop for a rare aviation moment in the past few days, with the world’s three core strategic heavy-lifting aircraft operating within the country.
Several large US military transport aircraft were spotted landing in Shenzhen over the weekend, widely seen as preparation for US President Donald Trump’s expected trip to the southern Chinese city for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) forum next week.
And on Monday, a Russian-made, Chinese-owned Il-76 transport plane...
title: C-17, Il-76 and Y-20 equals: an aviation moment in the skies over China

author: Cao Jiaxuan
description:
Manila’s efforts to strike a more conciliatory tone towards Beijing are unlikely to ease tensions in the contested South China Sea, a Chinese analyst has cautioned.
This was because the Philippine foreign ministry held minimal influence over actual maritime policy and enforcement operations, the South China Sea researcher said.
The assessment follows a rare public rebuke issued on Sunday by the Philippine ministry, cautioning officials against inflammatory rhetoric directed at China and calling...
title: Why Manila’s call for softer tone will not ease South China Sea tensions with Beijing

author: Chao Kong
description:
China’s high-performance rare-earth rubber faces a commercial test as manufacturers seek to expand its use in electric vehicle (EV) and heavy-duty tyres, with market data suggesting it commands a higher price than conventional synthetic rubber.
Rare-earth cis-butadiene rubber grade ND9106 was quoted at 22,500 yuan (US$3,400) per tonne in China during the week from October 26 to November 1, compared with 16,660 yuan per tonne for conventional BR9000 in Shandong province, according to market data...
title: China eyes new grip on EV sector with high-performance rare-earth rubber

author: Victoria Bela
description:
Chinese scientists have developed a first-of-its-kind purifier capable of removing breakaway tumour cells that circulate through the bloodstream, potentially preventing the recurrence and spread of some cancers.
The Shanghai Jiao Tong University-led team said the proof-of-concept platform could lower the risk of metastasis – the leading cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide – in a peer-reviewed research paper published on November 2.
When tested in mouse models of breast cancer, the device...
title: Chinese ‘black-hole’ purifier catches tumour cells in blood to stop cancer spread

author: Phoebe Zhang
description:
Fourteen people have been killed and dozens more hospitalised after a fire broke out in a high-rise building in northern China.
The fire broke out at around 5pm on Sunday in Taiyuan, the capital city of Shanxi province, according to the local Yingze district government. The fire was put out by around 7pm and rescue efforts ended at around 8.30pm, the authorities’ statement said.
That night, 38 people were sent to hospital, including five people who had died. By Monday morning, the death toll had...
title: Fire in northern China high-rise building kills 14, injures dozens more

description:

title: China’s torpedo tech, defects at Hong Kong MTR station: 5 weekend reads you missed

author: Gabriel Dominguez
description:
Recent mainland Chinese naval deployments in the western Pacific and South China Sea have raised questions over whether Beijing is rehearsing operations to stop US and allied forces from intervening in a Taiwan conflict, according to analysts.
Beijing has not announced any large-scale drill in relation to recent People’s Liberation Army (PLA) naval activities.
But a November 6 assessment by US-based think tank the Institute for the Study of War (ISW) said the PLA could be conducting a major...
title: Is the PLA rehearsing operations to keep US forces out of a Taiwan conflict?

author: Victoria Bela
description:
Chinese researchers have created a comfortable electrode for non-invasive brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) that achieved over 94 per cent accuracy in visual mind-typing tests during day-long use.
The gradient electrodes – designed to overcome the current trade-offs of conventional uniformly soft or rigid electrodes – were integrated into a commercial electroencephalogram (EEG) cap and tested during rest over the span of 14 hours.
Furthermore, the electrodes enabled eight hours of stable EEG...
title: China’s comfortable brain-reading device achieves 94% mind-typing accuracy in day-long use
